headline: NEW DETAIL follow-up to 0400-01 -- Trump claims ~85% of Iran's manufacturing capability is gone and the US can destroy 38 bridges'
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the 85% figure] 'Their [Iran's] manufacturing capability is reduced. It is basically about 85 per cent gone.
sources: US President Donald Trump -- White House briefing room remarks Nov 9 (85%) and CNN phone interview with Jim Sciutto Nov 8 (38 bridges)
fault_line: Is 85% a real Pentagon number -- or a number Trump invented on camera? The audience is already calling the percentages fake.

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the 85% figure] 'Their [Iran's] manufacturing capability is reduced. It is basically about 85 per cent gone. They are talking to us, and they are talking very politely, and we will see what happens,' Trump told reporters after meeting Qatar's PM (ANI via Daily Hunt, Nov 9 22:32Z; India TV; Open Magazine; Europe Says). Trump gave NO basis for the estimate in the remarks and did not specify which industries it covered (Open Magazine / Europe Says). The figure is Trump's claim, NOT an assessed fact -- no Pentagon, IAEA or independent confirmation has surfaced. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the 38 bridges] 'We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They'll all be down,' Trump told CNN on Sunday, adding he would rather not do it because 'it'll take 10 years to rebuild them' (CNN via Daily Caller / farazwire / Zark News). Power plants were also named as identified targets. The 38-bridges detail comes from the Sunday interview and was NOT recorded in any prior scan -- a missed catch-up. [CONTEXT] Trump also repeated that Iran 'cannot have a Nuclear Weapon -- That is non-negotiable!' and that Gulf partners prefer the status quo (blockade + Operation Iron Gate). The 85% claim sits alongside his earlier unverified figures from the same CNN interview: 301% inflation, 10% missile capacity and 15% drone capability remaining (farazwire / Zark News).
sections.what_verified: 1 countable tiered family: ANI (T1) carries the 85% claim. CNN is the originator of the 38-bridges quote but has NO declared tier in the registry and does not count. India TV, Open Magazine, Europe Says, Daily Caller, farazwire, Zark News carry the same quotes and have no declared tier. primary_source_single_family is TRUE -- both numbers are Trump's own words, and the claim keeps its PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM label.
sections.what_disputed: IAEA: Iran still holds approximately 440.9 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60% purity, below the ~90% weapons-grade level (Daily Caller citing IAEA/AP) -- the stockpile survives whatever '85% of manufacturing' means, and 60% material is the short step from weapons-grade. DNI Tulsi Gabbard told the Senate in March 2025 that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon, and in prepared March 2026 testimony maintained the 2025 strikes had obliterated the enrichment programme with no rebuild effort -- which undercuts the need for a new '85% gone' claim (Daily Caller). Trump gave no basis for 85% and did not define 'manufacturing capability'. The 38-bridges threat is a capability boast, not an observed action; no strikes on bridges have been reported.
sections.why_matters: Trump put two new numbers on the table -- 85% gone, 38 bridges in one hour -- and neither number has any evidence behind it. The IAEA's own figure says Iran still holds 441 kilos of 60% uranium.
sections.context: Background: NEW DETAIL follow-up to 0400-01 -- Trump claims ~85% of Iran's manufacturing capability is gone and the US can destroy 38 bridges in an hour; no basis given for either number

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump put two new numbers on the table -- 85% gone, 38 bridges in one hour -- and neither number has any evidence behind it. The IAEA's own figure says Iran still holds 441 kilos of 60% uranium. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is 85% a real Pentagon number -- or a number Trump invented on camera? The audience is already calling the percentages fake.
